model: I'd like to talk about my first manager, Linh, who hired me as a junior marketing assistant about three years ago. She's the kind of person who stays calm in every meeting, and she's still working at the same company, which is where I'm working too, so I see her most days. When I joined, I was really shy, and she basically took me under her wing. The important thing she taught me was to speak up. In my first few months I had ideas, but I kept them to myself because I was scared of sounding stupid. Then there was one project which went badly wrong, and I realised later that I'd spotted the problem weeks earlier but never mentioned it. So I learned the hard way. Afterwards, Linh sat down with me and gave me some really constructive feedback. She didn't blame me at all; she just said that a team only works when everyone who notices something says so. Honestly, that conversation was a turning point for me. What I admire is that she leads by example, because she admits her own mistakes in front of the whole team. Her words have really stuck with me. These days I'm the one who asks questions in meetings, and I'm even mentoring a new intern. I owe a lot to her, to be honest.
